I will performe my beſt in your behalfe ▪ But I doe feare I am not valiant Sir. Enter Niente. So our progeny may ſtill be kiſſes— If you retard your preſence whilſt the Sunne (In's race) fill vp one Howre, you'le find before Your next reuiew, that griefe hath made me old, And I ſhall looke more like a Matron then A Bride; ſo much your abſence mortifies. Like to my Genius he doth mooue about The houſe. Our ſoules are ſurely neere ally'd— The Garden (Signior) doth containe more walks, As penſatiue in ſhade as this. I doe Beſeech you, change your path, and leaue me heere. If I am ſeene, my life is forfeited— How dare I traficke thus For loue with thee: when thy accompts with Heauen Are yet not cleer'd that luſt betrai'd thee to? Were I well knowne Vnto the qualitie of thy new loue, I would reueale my ſelfe, and take from thy Beliefe the falſe opinion of my guilt. Beare witneſſe Immortalitie and Truth That I'm officiall heere but by pretence, My Vaines are cold and chaſte as Northerne ſnow. Scoperta is my name. I Siſter am To Altamont ; not Miſtreſſe of his luſt. And you when I beheld, I ſaid to Heauen, O make but his immortall part like to The Garment Nature clothes it in, and h • lle Remaine a Type, from whom ſhall be deriu'd The Prophets, and the Kings that rule the Earth. I ſhould haue vſ'd More leaſure and nice Art, when I did giue My loue away. Since time grew old, he ſlowly findes his ſteps I'th darke: by day he ſwifter moues. Get thee To bed; The Caſements of thine Eies are ſhut; Impriſ • ning their deare Light. Come my Sciolto, and confirme the vertue of Thy faith; or I diſperſe my Soule in Sighs, And make this Chaire my eaſie monument. Roads. You ſwelling Cloudes choake my afflicted ſight ▪ Nature (it ſeemes) is frighted from her health. I want pretence to ſooth my faith: Els I Would hope your hands depriued her not of breath? The howers that gaue her opportunitie To erre, were knowne ſo few; that my beliefe Concludes her guiltleſſe of the actuall ſinne. Be deafe (ſweete heauen) to this. Did Sciolto Iterate her foule ſpeech? Is he dead too? The Genius of the world Is ſicke, all Formes muſt ceaſe. O Sir, ſhould I reſtraine the flux, my Eies Would drop from their looſe Stringes inſtead of Teares. O Sciolto. Art thou ſo early fled, To taſt eternitie, and vnknowne fate. I bring My innocence, to'th'cleere ſuruay of Heauen. No mercie, for our Noble Mothers ſake? I am too weake to force from your beliefe Miſtakes ſo ſtrong. The laſt of all My merits ſhall be calld obedience to Your will: If you doe owe a kindneſſe to Your ſelfe; thinke on Religion and the Lawes. Exit. Pale Planet ſhine! It muſt be he. My Eares Perſwade me they oretooke his voice. Sir, Sir! — There's not a Starre in all the Firmament Belongs to vs. Our loue was of too nimble growth vnleſſe Philoſophie giue hope, that after death We may conuerſe; this is the laſt of all Our interuiewes. The word that's heard abreuiates our diſcourſe And li • e: the Sand that limits both is falne Into the reach of number now: and I Haue ſpent with thee the haſty time prefix'd For a deuout imployment of my Beades. The murderers are within. Vnto thy Lips I'ld throw a kiſſe; but with The ſtrings of my poore ſolitary Lute They' • e bound my hands! — And I could weepe vntill I quench'd that •• ame, And drew ſuſpition that a ſecond Flood Was come to drowne mortallitie agen! Whence is that noiſe? Hah, Sciolto ! And I ſuppoſ'd thee fled A Harbenger to Heauen: with purpoſe to Beſpeake my Billet neere to thine. We cannot (Sir) be mortall long; therefore Receiue a hope our ſufferance will ceaſe. So much of various fate, ſo ſoone expres'd Two louers yet nere knew; ſince ſimpathy Firſt dwelt on Earth. Whilſt ſtill ther's noiſe, and buſines in the world; Whilſt ſtill the warres grow loud, and battels ioyne; Whilſt Kings their Queenes ſalute in Iuory beds. Our Reaſon frights our Sences to diſtruſt. My Lipps doe beage from thine a Legacie— I'le not reſigne theſe bonds of Death, vnleſſe Sciolto ſhare in the compaſſion too— My memorie wou • d ſinne, ſhould it record Ought that might nouriſh my diſlike of you: You made me taſte of ſorrow, not of wrath.
What ſlaue diſturbs the quiet of my Eare?
That kiſſe (Sir) was ſo powerfull and moiſt, That you haue robd my Lips of all their wealth!
A keene Gueſt, inuited heere— I am come to get your children for you. This I conſider Sir, and therefore make Such haſte to mingle with your wife; that the Kinde world may haue ſome iſſue from my Loynes. If you aduance one inch beyond that ruſh I'le amble through the Streets, and blow your Dirge With the great Horne that growes vpon your Brow. S'light Sir; I come t'eaſe the labour of your Body; And you want courtſhip to returne me thanks. But what hereafter I Performe, ſhall be for your good Ladies ſake, And not for yours. Now Sir, you powre ſweet Caſſia in my Broath. My Blood affects to skirmiſh more With Ladies then with men. What would you ſpeake? Who told ye ſo? Not I beleeue it Sir! Sir I will doe't. Is your Lady fruitfull? I would be loath t'looſe my labour on her? O fie! You an Italian Sir, and thus Behaue the knowledge of diſgrace with lowd And popular diſlike? You thinke becauſe Y'are curſ'd, we'le allow you ſhort Hornes: I'le graft Vpon your head a paire ſo tall, they ſhall Goe neere to pricke the verie Planet (Sir) Thet rul'd at your natiuitie. Signior, goe! take downe a Cuſhion, and pray ▪ You cannot chooſe but know the frailty of The times: the ſurfeits of the wombe, and how Great Ladies doe relieue their Appetites. Your owne confeſſion of my parts commends Your wife in her ſage choice. There be that ſinne With feeble vſhers and the witherd Dwarfe. I merit better looks Sir, that muſt thraſh All night for ye, and without wages Sir! Had he the Deuill for's Phyſitian choſe, He could nere haue come by the like Cordiall.— Florence knowes me well: I'm call'd Sciolto, Your mercie and your kindneſſe (Lady) thus Aduance my ſhape; your pleaſure was I ſhould deſpiſe your husbands frownes, and I behau'd My ſelfe with terrour maſculine: but now We are peculiar and reſeru'd, I know Humilitie, a ſoft and quiet garbe; A diſtance that ſhall well become the ſtate So eminent and rich a beauty claimes. Madam, ſtore me with armes and weapons to Reſiſt his perſonall aſſault, and I Shall need no more protection then my ſelfe. Las! not mine! Tis true, that if I like my Oppoſite, I haue a tricke te giue an eaſie fall, And ſtand to't ſtifly too when I ha'done— Excuſe me Sir, th'are great by me! Madam—They are all wi'child! Blame the humorous Planets that orerule The blood. Ere yet this preſent Month expires; (Let's ſee—I,!) Some three and forty Ladies (Or there about) will quicken with male Twinnes. So wiſe Fame ſings. I will make bold to gather my firſt fruits— Goes to kiſſe her. How deare Lady? Death, I'm Sutor vnto Gallens widdow! Madam, I know it not becomes the high Demeanure of your birth to dance (iuſt like A Kid) to th'muſicke of each wind that blowes. Ere you admit of dalliance I ſhould vſe Some induſtry of Tongue, and flexure of the pliant Ioints, to court and wooe conſent. Only a little t'recreate the Chine— Haſt no good booke, whoſe comfortable vſe may fill th'expence of time? Any o'th Moderns. Rablays i'th praiſe of Midwiues. Aretine on copulation. Or th'Odes of Theophile vnto his whore. Thinke on the frailtie of The fleſh; and be not long vnmercifull— Charintha within. Siſter! Madam! And ſhall be ſtill ſo (Sir) vnleſſe your wife Diſmiſſe her pride, and vouchſafe to coole me. Take diſcipline awhile, Know if there be A boiſterous motion vſd, I haue for each Of you a round Synamon Plumme, and they Shall enter your nice ſtomacks the wrong way— What, as to copulate and increaſe kind? It has beene a vocation euer ſince The Sunne ſpi'd man thus crawling on the Earth— My curſes (Sir) haue cauſe t'aſſault Her more then yours: for ſhe has ſtaru'd me heere With want of naturall delight. My free Large growth and tincture of my haire denote, My conſtitution cannot ſuffer me, To weare a ſurpleſſe, or proceed Eunuch. Though I ſhould bath and ſwimme in Iulips Sir, I'ue ſtill vnrulie heate about my Chine. Haue I not equall reaſon to complaine? In three Houres not ſo much as a drie kiſſe. Th'old amorous Deacon that imbrac'd his Cow Was not ſo deſtitute. A Negro might be vſefull now, although Sh'ad but one eye, and that fix'd on her heele. Signior, preſume no more vpon a fond Eaſie nature. I haue beene abſtinent Too long. Haſte, and with pliant ſteps preſent Your wife; Ot elſe I'le aſſure ye you ſhall ſeeke Some other man to Cuckold ye for me. I thanke ye (Signior) but We Florentines doe ſleepe like Leuorites, With our Eyes open: how ere, I could vouchſafe To ſhoot you now, and preuent your kindneſſe.— I meant not to giue fire. There is a tricke of grauity i'th ſtate Cald Law. Beſides, you dead, the children which I chance to get vpon your buckſome wife, I ſhould goe neere to keepe at my owne charge. I'le to my chamber now, and fortifie There, I remaine (during the pleaſure of Your wife) your Tenant (Signior) in fee tayle. — Exit. Cals he her, his concubine? By this hand There's not a Prince in all the Eaſt, has ſuch Another. This Altamont ſtill gripes'em In the flanke; he knowes to chuſe his cattell. Be thou pleas'd, O yong and wholeſome Lady! The fumes of ſpicery? you muſt not now — I ſigh my firſt ſalute Was ſo intempratly perform'd. But O! The iuſtice of my Starres! My loue is now Reueng'd vpon my luſt. With pure chaſte flame I Court the Miſtreſſe vnto Altamont ; One heere reſeru'd for ſinfull vſe. Stay, ſtay!— Haſt thou not heard my vowes, whoſe violence And number well might ſatisfie ſuſpect in wayward Kings. With what aduice of modeſty canſt thou Accuſe my blood; when in this Manſion th'art Contain'd for the like ſinne? If ere I practiſe impious heate agen, Some long armd Fiend that in the Center dwels Reach at my foot, and pull me into flames. Thy name, and then my doubts I will forſake? O dire affinity! my loue is now Alli'd vnto my hate. Yet Altamont Nere merited my wrath. It is the wit The policie of ſinne, to hate thoſe men We haue abuſd. When firſt I ſpi'd the grace And luſture of thy ſhape; me thought I lou'd, And my ſicke heart enform'd me loue was good: Her beauties ſo increaſe; that they do make My comprehenſion poore. O ſtay, vntill my vowes Affoord a larger warrant of my faith— Goe noble Maid, wert thou diuided from My reach, by Sheets of Elementall fire, By ſtreames of recking blood, by purple miſts (Which Cannons in their acclamation breath) Or winds (when met to blow each other from The Earth) yet I would pull thee to my Heart. Falſe luſt, I take of thee eternall leaue— For what are theſe deſignd? Now am I As raſcally a ſinner, as euer. O Loue! A little grace. Shall we be wrap't in curlings intricate? And ſhall we 'tweene two ſhady Poplars hang I'th Indian-Net, whoſe ſlippery cloſures may Entangle vs ſo faſt, we n'ere ſhall be Vntied agen ▪ Yes, much! Not an inch.— And ſhall my action more. It mightineſſe And ſtate, taught me to faſt from fleſh; and now, I am well pleas'd to make't perpetuall Lent. Goe, kneele to your husband, and beg from him Lawfull recreation: My ſelfe intend To purchaſe a few Beades, and turne Vot'ry. She'le nere moue hence, 'till I'ue inrag'd her ſpleene. Why—ye are not handſome. Thy aged skull in ſtead of haire Oregrowne with Moſſe, and lookes as if t'had binne, A Thouſand yeares entoomb'd. Thy ſollitary Teeth, in diſtance ſtand Like the decayed Arches of a Bridge. Wilt not yet goe? Thy Fingers are all crook'd, like the Tallans Of a Griffon. Thou walkſt on Cloven-feete. Thy Bones are pil'd acroſſe ▪ Much like the Stickes on a Coniurers fire. It muſt not be. For with theſe two (of which I meane to rob your armorie) there ſhall Be paſſage forc'd broad enough for a Teeme Of Southerne Elephants. Farwell Oiſter! — Exit. I'le not be truſ'd (Sir) like a Pullet thus— Pare my nailes too.— There is ſome danger in this chance, my dull Heart beates with ſlow, and ominous leaſure. — Hah! Scoperta? A cruell deſtinie Ha •• murdred all our ioy. endeuouring an Add 〈◊〉 for ſtealth of thee, I was ſurpriſ'd, Diſa • md; euen heere 'ith preſence of my Starres. O none! Or if there be, Thei • influence is ſo weake that at This diſtance Babes may blow'em out. Sure ou • Creation we haue tooke vnknowne to Fate. That fatall Prophecie Will ſhake my Soule from out my fleſh; and like Some tame Hermit I ſhall vnwounded die. Grimme wild horrour! Haſt thou no weapons there that I may vſe T'anihilate their vigor and their ſhape? This ſudden eleuation of the Soule ▪ Preſageth death: as if it practis'd how To riſe, and climbe ere ſhe begins her flight. I'le be as calme as are Arabian winds. Scoperta, ſtay; Vnheard we will conuerſe. — O for the Giant race, to helpe me heaue Thoſe Mountaines vp; that I might burie this Proud Structure and my ſelfe! Yon burlie Oake (Whoſe Roots reach hell) I'le manage till I pownd And batter all the Marble into Flowre.— Speake what thou art? Not thy tame ſacrifice, but victorie I'le be. For naked as I am I will Reſiſt my death; and ſince vnfurniſh'd to Reuenge, yet I ſhall trouble thy beſt ſtrength.— Falſe tyranie! There's reliſh of intent! Miracle of bountie! With ſolemne penitence I could accuſe My crimes 'gainſt thee: but griefe's akinne to feare. This great demeanu • e of thy ſpleene diuides Th'intent of Gratitude. I know not which T'affoord thee moſt, my enuie, or my loue. A little reſpite giue,— Muſt we needs • ight? Yet ſtay! — Know I doe loue thy Siſter well. Stiffe as a columne! — I'le worke thy ſtrength ſo low, that Virgins ſhall Haue power to ſhakle thee with ſpinners Thrids— This cloſure hath Intangled vs, let's make another charge? Wilt thou not bleede? Not yet?—I skirmiſh with vnbodied Aire. That Wound gapes like to a yawning Giant. I reele Before thy breaſt, and ſtumble at a Wart— My wounds cloſ'd vp, what meanes this courteſy? Can thy young honour ſtoope to ſuch low flight? O ſooth my laſt ambition then ▪ be thou My Executioner. Thy ſpirit Altamont aſcended with The loue of all my chiefeſt orizons. Scoperta, O my Girle! I thought thy beauties had beene darke and cold, And th'adſt (ere this) begun an eaſie ſleepe Within thy ſilent Graue. Since this ſad night, did blind the drowſi • world, They thus haue manacled my ſtrength. They'ue watch'd My hardy violence ſo tame, that now Each featherd Forreſter rooſts in my Beard. I doe confeſſe m'imagination once Did ſinne againſt them both: but if it ere Extended vnto act; let me loſe Heauen ▪ If in thy functions, gentle Nature claime An intereſt, let vs imbrace, and vſe Solemnity, before we doe forſake Each others view. O Scoperta! this is the laſt of all Our buſie dreames; what we poſſeſſe is but Imaginary now: Thy ſhadow I, Embrace, not thee: for like to it, thou'lt flie From my enioyment, and no more be ſeene!— Ere long we muſt be cold, Cold, cold my Loue, and wrapp'd in ſtubborne ſheets Of lead: hows'd in a deepe, a gloomy vault; Where no ſociety will mix with vs, But what ſhall quicken from our tainted limmes. But O! how many Ages may ſucceed In Heauens darke Kalender; ere we agen Materiall be, and meet in our warme fleſh? Phyloſophie doth ſeeme to laugh vpon Our hopes, and wiſe Diuinity belies Our knowledge, with our Fayth: iealous Nature, Hath lock'd, her ſecrets in a Cabinet, Which Time nere ſaw: and he that in it prys Vnto Religion forfeites his bold Eies. O ſad acomp • . How is my bounty now Exhauſt: This is the laſt I ere ſhall giue— Slaues. Stretch now your Cordage out, Pull till my Eies do • ſtarte like Bulletts from my Skull, Murdering where they flie— This deceipt brings wonder, great as our ioy. They that diuide vs now, muſt vſe the ſtrength Of ſwelling floods, and helpe of Thunder too — Tis I, that haue moſt • eedfull vſe of your Kind charitie: forget my errors paſt, And to oblige my future gratitude Giue Hymen leaue to know your ſiſter for My wife. • y Vnkles death hath lent me power Still to maintaine her in ſuch qualitie As ſhall become my deere reſpects to you, The greatneſſe of her virtue, and her blood. You ſhall be precious to my eies as day.
The better ſhap'd I am (Sir) the more cauſe You'le find, to loue the Iſſue I ſhall get Vpon your wife.
He's great with Ladies of all ages, all Degrees.
Tis he Madam, and ſuch a he as muſt Be onely likened to himſelfe. I'm Charintha's woman Sir— If you ſhould chance (My honourd Lord) to drop thoſe trifles heere, I would be mannerly, and reach'em vp. Madam, ther's a new Dand • lo, a new Count, lighted at the Gate, and craues entrance. Which, when your Lordſhip does, Ile returne ye A pointed Diamond, big as a Steeple. My Lady'gins t'enquire (Sir) after ſleepe, For it growes late. Make the Deuill your Factor; Ther's a Stocke To ſet vp with. Flings it agen. Exit. The little God Hath lately prick'd her with his baudy ſhaft.
A Stone, a Stone! the thing growes, I'ue enow— Th'are ſuch your knowledge ſhall affect: they muſt Inioy what I atchieue. Dull men, o'war, The Trophie of my victorie behold, She's mine: bow, and doe homage to her lippe. —
But will your Lordſhip walke and ſee the ſpring? We haue a Garden where it euer dwels. Your trayne of Paraſite, Pimpe, Foole and Dwarfe, Speake you at firſt, to be the true yong Lord. Thou doſt requite the skornes which I did throw On thy firſt loue. My deſtiny muſt needs Be tragicke now: ſince the contracted ſcope Of all my ioy, reſts in diſeaſed hope. Exit ▪
I haue an odde humor, not to be kill'd.
Come ſweare, ſweare now (on this victorious ſword) Thou wilt obey th'iniunctions of my wrath, And yet in perſonall act, not mooue, but when My will appoints a mixture of thy ſtrength. Still thou doſt mourn ( Alteza ) like a Doue. Soft muſick ▪ Hearke, hearke how the Roman-Organ ſeemes T'inuoke the Thracian Lire; the Cymbals of Iudea, call Caſtilian -Cornets foorth, And German -Viols wake the Tuſcan Lute ▪ The ſacred noiſe attend, that whilſt wee heare, Our ſoules may dance into each others eare.
Be bold and meet your chance •
speeches.Charintha·: I'le ſmile no longer then theſe rich ſparkles Shine in my Eies. Enter Dandolo.
The Lady that is nam'd Charintha heere, muſt be reueald; for Il'd Exallt her Lippes, and make'em knowne to mine. I'le firſt doe ſpeciall grace vnto your Lip— My Penne hath woo'd you oft; but now by ſtealth Thus ſingle I'm arui'd, a Moone before The time I did prefix. T'was Winter when I ſpecifi'd the date Of my aproach, and then my blood was cold; But now the ſpring is come, Things would couple. Theſe (Lady) are very ſerculare Pearle— Doe you affect'em Lady? I am inſtructed then. That I did ill, to leaue my Pearles behind. Has not this houſe the priuiledge of peace? Hence, and be dead! Bid Kings winde ſilke, and Princes meaſure oats. D'you thinke y'are the Count? Thought's free. Sir, —you ſhall know, No man ere got me, but my owne Father. Exit. MY iourney was by ſtealth, elſe I had brought With theſe, Legions of Dukes to ſpeake my birth. My corporall method I will diſorder, ere I'le miſſe her view. This Britiſh Groate is thine; traficke for Pinnes. No bribes? I am belou'd. Th'are Nobles of a ſupreame race. This is Stocccata call'd, and that Punto. They both Are come to warrant my creation good Vpon the Gauntlet of a Giant or a Whale. Tumultuous fights the veſtments marre. Lady! behold two Worthies here; Dragons In fight. They come to preach my birth. Th'are knowne to Fame. I ſay th'are Potentates; and they doe awe— I doe oppugne the motion with my ſcorne. Pardon me Sir! I ſay't alowd; The prowdeſt wight on Earth Shall not kicke me, excepting your deare ſelfe. Agreed, Six Duck • ts you ſhall number more. Good faith (Sir) for no harme. Theſe thouſand yeeres 't has b • n obſeru'd, th'eldeſt Brothers of her houſe (Sir) could nere endure To cut their Throates. With ſapi • nt Arts, we will proiect to ſaue Th'reputation of your i • ſtice. I will promulgate I am dead, and both, My Champions heere ſhall ſw •• r't. Ranſome, I'le giue: for I doe hate to die.

What, is that ſawcy Groome? Does he ſell Egges? Beauties, were you • hands cleane, they ſhould be kil • 〈◊〉 .
Sir a word. Me thinks you looke, like raw Porke.
speeches.Scoperta:: Our new ſociety muſt not be ſeene. But if thy loue be free from carnall Arts, (Such as the curled Youth of Italy Doe vſe) make me thy ſudden ſtealth ▪ Early, (Ere the ſucceeding Sunne ariue i'th'Eaſt) Appeare beneath my Caſements view, and I Will follow thee along the ſpacious World.
Queſtion your Glaſſe! Your Face was caru'd—out of A Blew Cabidge; and 'tis contracted now To one, oblique Wrinkle.
Were we his heires, w'had cauſe to haſten his Deceaſe.
Maintaine your birth—Were you my fathers Bawdes?
Alas, you are young (Sir) you know not vs! We cannot ſwell and rant like things that would Be rather heard then felt: but we can thruſt Our Whineards home, with ioy and quiet too. Stay, woo't thou kill him (Punto) or ſhall I? Fie Sir. Draw your weapon in a Ladies Chamber? You ſtill diſplaie a courage ill Brought vp, moſt vainlie nurturd (Sir) beleeue't. Heare Sir th'aduice of an old ſhot. I'ue hit The marke more then once in my time, and tam'd Many a mad Boy too. If either of's Vouchſafe to greete ye with a hand or foot, Take it, and be thankfull: le • t by returne Of wrath, worſe doe enſue. Steele of Toledo is all we manage— He has but thinne Philoſophie that cannot ſuffer this — Wele venture one Commandement to ſaue another ſir. Slight Sir, I nere was in Elizium, I. Nor ſhould I finde the way thither, though Signior Argos, lent me Nintie Nine of his Eies.
Sweet heart; you are not read i'th'rudiments Of wrath. You ſhall perceiue ſome that are lowd And actiue with their Lungs; Courage in them You may ſuſpect: but when you ſee a coole And ſilent anger like to ours, then keepe Your wandring hands at home. Soft Sir, beware! I'ue buiſneſſe now of a more ſerious garbe. Diſpatch him thy ſelfe. Earlie to morrow I'le doe as much for thee on the two Zwits. Forbid it Heauen; but you ſhould haue free ſpace T'imploy your beſt ſtrength in your defence. But Sir, 'tis ſober patience makes vs ſafe. If now on eithers Haunch you did conferre A kicke; our ſecret wiſedome would direct Vs how to beare it for the time, and in Our owne aduantage too. He's young, Stoccata, carue him gentlie vp! — O Sir, your vallor ſtill imports ſome want Of a diſcreet and temperate breeding. Signior, you ſtill forget The quiet and the courteous wayes of ſpleene. You ſee we ſtill are calme — Enhaunce our pay, we'le kill him in the da • ke. Good Signior, any curteſie but this You may command. You ſtill doe moſt preſume Vpon the calmeſt, and th'eaſie Nature.
Keepe your ſword warme, it 'longs to the ſcabbard—
Madam, it muſt be he. I'ue tane a ſtrict Suruay of's Noſe; 'tis ſo like Altamonts.
O my forward bountie! There's but ſicke hope My Iewels will returne; ſince cuſtome ſhewes; What Ladies thus from ther dull Sutors get They doe preſerue as Tribute to their wit.
The longer moitie of the Night's vnſpent. Madam, good night. Exit.
May ſome kinde Saint, weepe o're your Soule vntill With holy dew, he waſh this ſinne away.
This ioy will make my Heart dance in my Breaſt.— They come, they come, deare loue, for euermore farewell ▪ And whether that our ſoules, when they're prefer'd To taſte eternity will euer thinke Vpon the bargaines of our humane loue, Is vnto me a deſolate ſuſpence.
speeches.Scoperta: Is there in all your vaines, no drop (vnmix'd With Gaule) that from our Mother is deriu'd, And ſo may tempt compaſſion from your Breaſt?
speeches.Sciolto: O my hot rage! I could Spit fire till I enkindle yonder Groue, Raiſing a flame that might perplex the Earth, And make'em thinke Heauen had dropp'd a Planet.
You haue oreheard, what will your knowledge grieue. Great Altamont (your Lord) who ſtill was prompt To curbe th'incitements of your wrath; threw wiſe Aduantage from his reach, and ſtruggled with The bold Sciolto, in an equall warre. Wiſe Heauen did mocke your Altamont : for whilſt Ore ioy'd with victory, he ſpies in's Breaſt A large deepe wound, and thence his Soule tooke flight.
speeches.Altamont: So hot is thy laſciuious blood, that as I ſprinkle it, it ſcaldes my hands—
• haue ſome courage yet, le • t in my Teeth, If thou art kinde, come neerer with my Throate—
speeches.Sciolto ▪: Scoperta, ſtay. My Soule ſhall houer ſtraite With thine. Stay for me in the Milky-path.
speeches.Dandolo: The motion I d • ſlike, 'tis dangerous.
